portfolio.name: Long-term Portfolio Thesis Tracker
portfolio.principle: Track whether the reason for ownership remains intact; do not let normal price volatility dictate thesis status.

holdings.name: Vanguard FTSE All-World UCITS ETF
holdings.thesis: Global equity foundation with broad geographic diversification and low-maintenance long-term exposure.
mustRemainTrue: Fund continues to provide broad global diversification.
Index methodology and fund structure remain appropriate.
Costs and tracking remain reasonable.
Long-term equity risk remains acceptable for the investment horizon.
sellTriggers: Material structural change to the fund/index that no longer fits the strategy.
Personal financial circumstances or risk tolerance change materially.
A clearly superior long-term core structure is deliberately adopted.

holdings.name: Vanguard S&P 500 ETF
holdings.thesis: Broad exposure to profitable US large-cap companies and long-term US earnings growth.
mustRemainTrue: US large-cap earnings power remains structurally strong.
Index remains diversified enough for its role.
US concentration remains acceptable within the overall portfolio.
sellTriggers: A deliberate strategic move away from US equities.
Portfolio concentration becomes inappropriate for the user's risk capacity.
Fund/index structure materially changes.

holdings.name: Invesco QQQ Trust
holdings.thesis: Concentrated exposure to large technology and growth businesses benefiting from digitalisation and AI investment.
mustRemainTrue: Mega-cap technology earnings remain strong.
AI and technology investment continues translating into business value.
Valuation and concentration remain tolerable for the satellite allocation.
sellTriggers: Structural deterioration in mega-cap tech earnings or competitive position.
Concentration becomes incompatible with the intended risk level.
Long-term growth thesis materially weakens.

holdings.name: VanEck Semiconductor ETF
holdings.thesis: Higher-conviction semiconductor exposure capturing AI infrastructure, compute, memory and foundry demand.
mustRemainTrue: AI infrastructure demand remains strong over the long term.
Semiconductor industry earnings and capex remain healthy.
The semiconductor cycle does not become dominated by structural overcapacity.
Concentration and overlap with NVDA/TSM remain acceptable.
sellTriggers: Multiple independent indicators show a durable collapse in semiconductor demand.
Structural overcapacity causes sustained margin/return deterioration.
Portfolio overlap makes the satellite position unnecessarily concentrated.

holdings.name: NVIDIA
holdings.thesis: High-conviction exposure to accelerated computing, AI infrastructure and NVIDIA's hardware/software ecosystem.
mustRemainTrue: AI compute demand remains strong.
NVIDIA retains meaningful accelerator competitiveness and ecosystem strength.
Data-center growth remains economically attractive.
Margins and cash generation remain strong enough to support the valuation.
Competition and custom accelerators do not materially erode the moat.
sellTriggers: Sustained material loss of accelerator share without credible recovery path.
AI infrastructure spending structurally weakens for an extended period.
Gross margin/cash economics deteriorate materially and durably.
CUDA/software ecosystem advantage materially erodes.
Capital allocation materially undermines the investment thesis.

holdings.name: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.
holdings.thesis: High-conviction exposure to leading-edge semiconductor manufacturing and growing AI/HPC demand.
mustRemainTrue: Leading-edge node demand remains strong.
TSMC maintains technology and yield leadership.
AI/HPC demand supports utilisation, margins and returns on capital.
Customer diversification remains healthy.
Geopolitical and geographic concentration remains an acceptable risk.
sellTriggers: Sustained loss of leading-edge technology leadership.
Durable deterioration in AI/HPC demand or utilisation.
Material and persistent margin/return deterioration.
Competitive position versus Samsung/Intel materially improves against TSMC.
Geopolitical risk changes the risk/reward enough that the position no longer fits.

overlap.note: Multiple holdings benefit from the same AI investment cycle.
US technology exposure is larger than ticker count alone suggests.
Direct and indirect semiconductor exposure is concentrated here.
VWRA diversifies the portfolio but still contains many large US companies.
TSMC-specific exposure also appears indirectly in diversified funds.
Satellite positions lean toward higher-growth expectations.
